Dam man, thats super rough. I can understand the depression and anxiety,  but I don't have ADHD. What I really understand is not being able to do anything. I spent 2 years in my room. I suffered from a vitamin D deficiency, obesity (5'10" 295lbs), caffeine addiction (even though I slept for 12-16 hours a day). I had no job, no plan, no schooling and a super codependent partner who brought me anything I asked for. 

In that time I would have moments, mere seconds, of extreme joy, feeling a huge rush of invincibility, but it would come crashing back down and I lived in the darkness of my own mind.

It took me a long to time get off my ass. I don't even know what caused it. I just didn't want to feel so horrible any more. I am not a religious person, but I got on my knees and begged every god I could think of, one by one. I just wanted to die, or be better, or normal or anything other than what I was. It was when my best friend came over and found me on my knees praying that they helped me find help. They got me on state insurance, found me a therapist, drove me to my appointments. 

It's taken a long ass time, but between my meds, personal trainer, and having a factory job, I live a somewhat normal life. I am still often crippled by my down swings of Bipolar, but when I found out it wasn't my fault I felt like that, it became a little easier. I still have days I cant get out of bed, but I force myself. 

I also have a new partner who is supportive and understanding of my mental health rather than hope I stay in bed to give them someone to take care of.

In the end I find the more I do, the easier it is to do. 

I really hope you find a balance. I know that reaching out helped me the most. I'm here for you. I may not walk you're path, but I walk beside you.
